title: Divine Faithfulness
english: The Son of God, born from the seed of David according to the flesh, was designated as the Son of God in power according to the spirit of holiness from the resurrection of the dead.
This designation is not just a matter of power, but also of truth and nature.
As the Son of God, he is the archetype, and we, who are sons by position, are like images towards him.
Through him, we also become sons, and we are enriched by his Spirit through holy baptism, which allows us to call God 'Abba, Father' without hesitation.
The eternal power and divinity of God are also evident in creation.
The creator of things that are perishable and have been called into existence in time must be imperishable and eternal.
The question arises whether the unfaithfulness of some individuals will nullify God's faithfulness.
Those who were foreknown and received the law as a tutor, and had promises concerning Christ, are more honored than the others.
The Savior Himself said that He was sent only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel (Romans 1:3-4), and they became the firstfruits of those who were saved through faith.
If some people were lost due to their foolishness in believing, would God's truthfulness be nullified?
Certainly not, for the Father sent the Son from heaven, and although not all people believed in Him, this does not undermine God's faithfulness.
On the contrary, let God be true and every person a liar.
Instead of being considered true and spoken of as such, let the accusation of lying be attributed to humanity.
For God's nature is unchangeable and immutable, but human nature has been greatly shaken, and every person has become a liar to some extent.
The lie, which is sin, sometimes overpowers human thought, and human nature accepts this kind of disease.
It is not right to think or say such things about the God who rules all things.
Therefore, the accusation that human nature can suffer from lies, that is, from false thoughts, will be true.

But the man Emmanuel would not thus have it; for he was born from the seed of David according to the flesh, and is considered as one of us as a son of God because of his humanity, yet he is truly the Son of God in power and truth according to nature, through whom we also become sons.
If it is true to say that we have been enriched by his Spirit through holy baptism, then we also say 'Abba, Father' without hesitation.
